metaDescription: Six cordless and corded string trimmers under $100 compared on swath, battery capacity, edging, weight and line feed, with what this budget cuts.
expertTake: The CRAFTSMAN V20 trimmer and edger kit is our top pick under $100 because a 13 inch swath and a 4 Ah battery claim up to 63 minutes in a platform with many other tools. The goodjob 20V two battery kit is the value pick at the lowest tier. Skip this price band if you want to cut dense brush or maintain more than a small to medium yard, because those jobs need a 40V or gas trimmer that costs more.
introParagraphs: A string trimmer under $100 is a lightweight cutter for edging a lawn and knocking back weeds along fences. At this price you can have a battery model or a corded one that never runs out. What the cap removes is power: no brushless motor on most, small batteries and thin shafts.

That is fine for small yards, but it matters how you buy. Battery capacity, line feed type and weight decide whether the trimmer gets used. Listing prices move, so the $100 cap reflects Amazon prices when this guide was updated. We evaluated these trimmers from spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, and none of it replaces the maker's safety instructions.

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Light yard work on a small lot

products.description:
The goodjob is a 20V cordless trimmer that weighs just 3.5 lb and ships with two 2.0 Ah lithium batteries and a quick charger. The listing says it converts from a string trimmer to an edger and a weed cutter, and the 12 inch swath is a standard size for this class. Two batteries let you swap in a fresh one when the first runs out.

The tradeoff is that 2.0 Ah is a small pack, so each battery runs for a short session. Against the CRAFTSMAN, which lists a 4 Ah battery and up to 63 minutes, the goodjob has less runtime per pack but offers a spare. Against the WeGofly, it has smaller batteries and a narrower swath. Against the BLACK+DECKER corded trimmer, it is cordless but less powerful. It sits at the lowest tier.

Charge both batteries before a yard session. Replace the string when it frays and trim only dry grass, since wet grass drags the head and drains the cells. Clean the head and guard after each use, and store the batteries indoors out of the heat.

products.name: ALSO GO 24V cordless trimmer, 2 x 4.0 Ah, telescopic pole, 5 in 1 blades

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Mixed small yard jobs and tall or short users

products.description:
The ALSO GO is a 24V cordless trimmer with two 4.0 Ah batteries, a telescopic pole that adjusts from 33 to 47 inches and five replaceable blade types, including a wheel for edging. It weighs about 3.28 lb and is described as splash proof, which helps when you trim in damp grass.

The telescopic pole is the standout, since a one size shaft is awkward for tall and short users. The multi blade design adds versatility but also adds parts to lose and to keep sharp. Against the WeGofly 4 in 1, it offers a pole length range and a smaller battery pair. Against the CRAFTSMAN, it has bigger spares but a less established platform. It sits in the middle tiers.

Set the pole length so your arm is slightly bent when you hold the head near the ground. Keep the blades clean and sharp, and swap in the right head for each job rather than forcing a string head through brush. Charge the batteries before a long session and store them away from heat.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A corded trimmer like the BLACK+DECKER at 6.5 amp never runs out of power but is tied to an outlet and an extension cord. A cordless trimmer like the CRAFTSMAN, WORX or goodjob moves freely but limits you to battery runtime. Under $100 the corded model gives more raw power per dollar. The common mistake is buying cordless for a yard that is mostly near an outlet.

The CRAFTSMAN lists a 4 Ah battery and up to 63 minutes, the WeGofly lists two 6.0 Ah batteries, the ALSO GO lists two 4.0 Ah batteries and the goodjob lists two 2.0 Ah batteries. More amp hours and a spare battery matter more than voltage at this price. A single small battery stops the job halfway through a yard.

A 12 inch swath, as on the WORX and goodjob, takes more passes than a 14 inch swath on the corded BLACK+DECKER. Auto feed or Command Feed, as on the WORX and BLACK+DECKER, saves bumping the head. A bump feed head is simple but wastes line. Wider swath and auto feed save time in a larger yard.

The goodjob weighs 3.5 lb and the ALSO GO 3.28 lb, which keeps fatigue low. A trimmer with a heavy battery at the back balances better than a motor head heavy tool. Check the shaft length, since a short shaft makes tall users stoop. A telescopic pole, as on the ALSO GO, fixes that.

Under $100 you give up brushless motors, 40V power and thicker shafts. A trimmer at this tier clears grass and light weeds well but struggles with dense brush and woody stems. Expect to replace the line often. If you have a large or overgrown yard, the cheap class will frustrate you.

Do not give up a spare battery or a comfortable grip to save a small amount. It is fine to give up a telescopic pole, an extra blade and a fancy head. A trimmer that hurts your wrist stays in the shed.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: The CRAFTSMAN, WORX, WeGofly, ALSO GO and goodjob move freely but depend on a battery.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The BLACK+DECKER never runs out of power but needs an outlet and a cord.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded if your yard is near an outlet, and cordless if you move across a larger lot.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A trimmer under 4 lb, a spare battery or a cord that reaches and auto feed to save bumping. Trim dry grass for best results.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WORX is the lightest simple choice, and the CRAFTSMAN gives the longest stated runtime.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have dense brush, a large yard or want brushless power and a 40V platform. Those start above this cap.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim grass edges and light weeds on a small to medium lot. The six here cover that.

faq.q: Is a string trimmer under $100 good enough?
faq.a: For grass edges and light weeds, yes. You give up brushless power and a 40V platform. Dense brush needs a stronger trimmer.

faq.q: Cordless or corded at this price?
faq.a: Corded gives more power per dollar and never runs out, but ties you to an outlet. Cordless is freer but limited by battery. Choose by yard layout.

faq.q: How long will the battery last?
faq.a: It varies. The CRAFTSMAN lists up to 63 minutes. Runtime falls in thick or wet grass, so treat the figure as a best case.

faq.q: What do I give up compared with a 40V trimmer?
faq.a: Power, runtime and the ability to cut thick weeds. You keep a lightweight trimmer for edges.

faq.q: How do I make the string last?
faq.a: Trim dry grass, keep the head clear of rocks and fences and replace line when it frays. Store spools out of the sun.
